title: Perf-canary metrics validation (runtime logs vs aggregated metrics) — working notes
content:
Purpose
- This doc is a scratchpad for validating perf-canary metrics correctness and label completeness.
- Specifically: spot-check that what we see in runtime logs/traces for canary requests matches what lands in aggregated metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, request counts), and that label schema is stable + within cardinality budget.
- Goal is to close known gaps before phase-1 rollout expansion (us-east -> eu-west) and before paging is enabled broadly.

Context / what we’re validating
- Canary traffic is tagged source=perf-canary (or equivalent request class) and should emit:
  - latency timing (prefill, decode, overall; streaming + non-streaming)
  - throughput tokens/sec (with correct streaming semantics)
  - runtime_build / git_sha, runtime_version
  - scheduler_mode
  - gpu_sku
  - model + model_version (or a single canonical model_id)
  - batch stats (prefill/decode counts, batch size, seq lens)
  - kernel selection (selected kernel id + fallback reason) — gated behind canary tag

- Known risk areas we’re watching:
  - streaming first-token timestamp alignment (historical bug)
  - label drops in ingestion pipeline / relabel rules
  - p95 window mismatch between runtime emitter and telemetry aggregation
  - missing/empty label values causing series explosions or mis-aggregation
  - “silent” sampling (metrics sampled but logs not, or vice versa) leading to confusing comparisons

Validation methodology (quick + reproducible)
1) Pick a small validation window (10–20 min) with steady canary traffic.
2) Pull a handful of canary request IDs from runtime logs (or trace IDs) for one slice.
3) For each request, record:
   - request start/end timestamps
   - prefill_ms, decode_ms, total_ms (if present)
   - prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens
   - streaming=true/false
   - model_id
   - runtime_build (sha)
   - scheduler_mode
   - gpu_sku
4) For the same time window, query aggregated metrics for the identical slice and compare:
   - request count aligns (within expected sampling / drop rate)
   - p50/p95 ballpark matches distribution from sampled requests
   - tokens/sec matches computed tokens/(decode time) with the agreed definition

NOTE: This is “sanity validation” not full statistical proof. We’re looking for obvious mismatches (e.g., 20–30% errors, missing labels, inverted semantics) and repeating patterns.

Environment / slices used in spot checks (so far)
- Region: us-east (phase 1)
- GPU: A100-80GB (majority), some H100 observed in mixed pools
- Models (current validation focus):
  - llama-3.1-70b-instruct (high throughput, stable)
  - qwen2.5-32b-instruct (sensitive to scheduler changes)
  - mistral-large (more variance; used for streaming check)
- Scheduler modes (explicit):
  - default
  - pinned_no_exp_heuristic_x (canary pinning to reduce variance)

Spot check #1 — non-streaming latency p95 (looks OK)
Date: 2026-02-02
Window: 17:10–17:25 UTC
Slice: region=us-east, model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct, gpu_sku=A100-80GB, scheduler_mode=pinned_no_exp_heuristic_x

Runtime log sample (n=30 requests)
- total_ms median ~ 820 ms
- total_ms p95 (rough from sample) ~ 980–1050 ms
- prefill_ms ~ 120–160 ms typical
- decode_ms ~ 650–850 ms typical
- completion_tokens mostly 256

Aggregated metric check (same window)
- canary_request_count: matches within ~5% (expected due to log sampling + retries)
- latency_p95_total_ms: ~ 1012 ms
- latency_p50_total_ms: ~ 835 ms

Notes
- This is the first slice where things “line up” closely.
- Good sign that p95 windowing is consistent for total latency in the non-streaming path.

Spot check #2 — streaming tokens/sec mismatch (FOUND BUG → fixed)
Date: 2026-02-03
Window: 09:40–09:55 UTC
Slice: region=us-east, model=mistral-large, gpu_sku=A100-80GB, streaming=true

Observed symptom
- Runtime logs show decode duration measured from request_start (includes prefill + waiting) for streaming path in one code path; aggregated metric computed tokens/sec using first_token_ts in another.
- Result: tokens/sec in metrics looked ~15–25% lower than what per-request logs suggested.

Example request (from runtime logs)
- prompt_tokens=768
- completion_tokens=256
- request_start=09:46:12.120
- first_token_ts=09:46:12.410
- last_token_ts=09:46:13.980
- decode_duration_from_first_token ~= 1570 ms
- tokens/sec (expected) ~= 256 / 1.57 = 163 tok/s
- tokens/sec (observed in metric series) ~= 128–140 tok/s

Likely root cause
- tokens/sec computation in streaming path using start_ts rather than first_token_ts for some spans.

Status
- Fixed by runtime PR: GitHub:redwood/pr_39157 (alignment on first-token timestamp)
- Action: After rollout of that runtime build, re-run this spot check to confirm metric series shifts upward accordingly.

Spot check #3 — missing gpu_sku label in ~8–12% of series (NEEDS FIX)
Date: 2026-02-05
Window: 20:00–20:20 UTC
Slice: region=us-east, model=qwen2.5-32b-instruct, scheduler_mode=default

What we expected
- Every canary request should resolve gpu_sku from node metadata and set gpu_sku={A100-80GB|H100-80GB|…}.

What we saw
- In aggregated metrics, ~8–12% of request_count shows up with gpu_sku="" (empty string) rather than missing label.
- This breaks filtering and makes tokens/sec/latency charts noisy because the empty-label series floats across GPU types.

Hypotheses
- Node metadata not available at emitter time for some requests (startup/refresh race).
- Relabel rule defaulting missing label to empty string.
- Some requests routed through a path that bypasses the GPU metadata attach (e.g., error/fast-fail path).

Evidence
- Runtime logs for affected request IDs show node_id present but gpu_sku missing in the structured log blob.
- Trace shows attribute gpu.sku absent for those requests.

Proposed fix path
- Runtime side (Omar/Julian): ensure gpu_sku is set for canary requests before span emission; if unavailable, set gpu_sku="unknown" (NOT empty string) to keep aggregation consistent.
- Telemetry side (Caleb/Thomas): update ingestion to drop empty-string labels or rewrite to "unknown" to avoid accidental “blank” series.

Owner / tracking
- File under ENG-2844 (runtime instrumentation) + ENG-2845 (metrics pipeline)
- Add a unit/integration test for label non-emptiness: GitHub:redwood/pr_39211 is the right place to extend.

Spot check #4 — p95 aggregation window mismatch (FOUND + HOTFIXED)
Date: 2026-02-06
Window: 14:30–15:10 UTC

Symptom
- Canary alert prototype flagged a p95 regression, but raw per-request logs didn’t show a corresponding distribution shift.

Root cause
- p95 aggregation window mismatch between runtime-emitted histogram buckets and telemetry pipeline rollup window (runtime was effectively being read at 10m, detector assumed 5m, causing partial-window artifacts during deploy + warmup).

Status
- Hotfix merged: GitHub:redwood/pr_39249
- Follow-up: re-run backtest after the fix to confirm alert volume drops during deploy windows.

Cardinality / label schema sanity checks
What labels we believe are allowed (current agreement)
- Required dimensions for perf-canary dashboards:
  - model_id
  - region
  - gpu_sku
  - runtime_build (or runtime_version; but not both at high frequency)
  - scheduler_mode
  - streaming (true/false)

- Optional (gated / sampled / debug-only):
  - kernel_id, kernel_fallback_reason
  - batch_max_seq_len, batch_prefill_count, batch_decode_count (careful: numeric -> should bucket or export as summary)

Findings
- kernel_fallback_reason has high cardinality in free-form string form (some reasons include interpolated values).
  - Recommendation: map to a small enum (e.g., UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE, AUTOTUNE_DISABLED, OOM_GUARD, UNKNOWN) and keep full string only in logs.
- scheduler_mode looks stable (low cardinality) provided we keep it to a named set, not a JSON blob.

Sampling / drop rate notes
- Runtime logs are sampled and may omit some requests; aggregated metrics should not be sampled (or should be sampled with explicitly exported sampling_rate).
- We currently have confusion in comparisons because:
  - logs: sampled at ~1:10 for canary in one service
  - metrics: unsampled but delayed

Action
- Add a metric “canary_metrics_sampling_rate” or a constant attribute in metrics metadata (even if 1.0) so people don’t assume equivalence.
- In the meantime, all spot checks should compare ratios/ballparks, not exact request-by-request counts.

Validation checklist (WIP)
For each region/model/streaming mode we expand to:
- [ ] request_count present and non-zero for expected canary cadence
- [ ] p95_total_ms within reasonable range vs last 7d median (no massive drift)
- [ ] tokens/sec matches per-request computed values within ~10% (after streaming fix)
- [ ] gpu_sku non-empty; “unknown” allowed but should be <1%
- [ ] runtime_build present and matches current deploy annotation
- [ ] scheduler_mode present and in allowed set
- [ ] no unexpected high-cardinality labels (kernel_reason, prompt_id, request_id MUST NOT be metric labels)

Open issues / to fix
1) Empty gpu_sku label series (see Spot check #3)
   - Severity: high (breaks slicing + dashboard trust)
   - Owners: Omar El-Sayed (runtime), Caleb Johnson (ingestion)

2) kernel_fallback_reason cardinality
   - Severity: medium (cost + noise; can block expansion)
   - Owners: Thomas Baird (cardinality), Hiro Tanaka (kernel export schema)

3) tokens/sec definition documentation
   - Severity: medium (people interpret differently; can cause false regression calls)
   - Ask: write down the canonical formula used by detector:
     - streaming: completion_tokens / (last_token_ts - first_token_ts)
     - non-streaming: completion_tokens / decode_duration_ms
   - Owner: Nadia Rahman

4) Verify scheduler pinning labels in metrics
   - We need to distinguish “pinned_no_exp_heuristic_x” from default; confirm it’s not being dropped by relabeling.
   - Owner: Julian Moore

Notes for dashboards (FYI for Felix)
- If we keep gpu_sku="" around, panels with “All GPUs” look fine but any filtered panel misleads.
- Suggest dashboard default filter excludes gpu_sku="" and includes gpu_sku="unknown" with an annotation (until fixed).

Next validation runs (planned)
- 2026-02-11: re-run streaming tokens/sec check after runtime build containing PR_39157 is fully rolled out in us-east.
- 2026-02-12: run same battery in eu-west once phase-2 canary starts (at least 2 models) — watch for new GPU SKUs and region label correctness.

Appendix: example queries / pseudo-queries (not canonical)
- Request count (slice)
  - sum(rate(perf_canary_requests_total{region="us-east", model_id="llama-3.1-70b-instruct"}[5m])) by (gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, streaming)

- Latency p95 (total)
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(perf_canary_request_latency_ms_bucket{region="us-east"}[5m])) by (le, model_id, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, streaming))

- Tokens/sec (series)
  - sum(rate(perf_canary_completion_tokens_total{...}[5m])) / sum(rate(perf_canary_decode_seconds_total{...}[5m]))

(We should keep these examples aligned with whatever lands in the final metric spec; these are here to make validation reproducible for engineers doing spot checks.)
